sentences.zh: 太祖武皇帝，諱克用，本姓朱耶氏，其先隴右金城人也。

translations.literal: Supreme Ancestor Martial Emperor, taboo name Keyong, originally surnamed Zhuye; his forebears were men of Jincheng in Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Ancestor Martial Emperor, personal name Keyong, was born of the Zhuye clan; his ancestors came from Jincheng in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 始祖拔野，唐貞觀中為墨離軍使，從太宗討高麗、薛延陁有功，為金方道副都護，因家於瓜州。

translations.literal: Founding ancestor Baye, in Tang Zhenguan served as Mori Army commissioner; following Taizong in campaigns against Goguryeo and the Xueyantuo he had merit, was made Deputy Protector-General of the Jin-fang Circuit, and took residence at Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor Baye served as Mori Army commissioner under Zhenguan; he followed Taizong against Goguryeo and the Xueyantuo, was rewarded as deputy protector of the Jin-fang Circuit, and settled his family at Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗平薛延陁諸部，於安西、北庭置都護屬之，分同羅、仆骨之人，置沙陁都督府。

translations.literal: Taizong pacified the Xueyantuo tribes, placed protectors at Anxi and Beiting subject to them, divided the Tongluo and Pugu peoples, and established the Shatuo Chief Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong subdued the Xueyantuo, he set protectors at Anxi and Beiting, assigned the Tongluo and Pugu to them, and founded the Shatuo Chief Commandery.

sentences.zh: 蓋北庭有磧曰沙陁，故因以為名焉。

translations.literal: For Beiting had a desert tract called Shatuo, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: A desert tract at Beiting was called Shatuo, and the name followed from that.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，以拔野為都督，其後子孫五世相承。

translations.literal: In Yonghui, Baye was made chief; thereafter descendants held the post for five generations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yonghui, Baye became chief; five generations of his line succeeded one another.

sentences.zh: 曾祖盡忠，貞元中，繼為沙陀府都督。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Jingzhong, in Zhenyuan, succeeded as Shatuo prefectural chief.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jingzhong became Shatuo prefectural chief in the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 既而為吐蕃所陷，乃舉其族七千帳徙於甘州。

translations.literal: Soon after he was trapped by the Tibetans; he then moved his clan, seven thousand tents, to Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans soon overran him; he led seven thousand tents of his clan to relocate at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 盡忠尋率部眾三萬東奔，俄而吐蕃追兵大至，盡忠戰歿。

translations.literal: Jingzhong soon led thirty thousand of his following east in flight; presently Tibetan pursuers came in force and Jingzhong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong soon fled east with thirty thousand followers; Tibetan pursuit caught up and he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 祖執宜，即盡忠之長子也，收合餘眾，至於靈州，德宗命為陰山府都督。

translations.literal: Grandfather Zhiyi, Jingzhong's eldest son, gathered the remnant following, reached Lingzhou, and Dezong appointed him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhiyi, Jingzhong's eldest son, rallied the survivors, reached Lingzhou, and Dezong made him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元和初，入為金吾將軍，遷蔚州刺史、代北行營招撫使。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhe he entered court as Golden Crow general, was transferred to prefect of Wei, and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he became a Golden Crow general, then prefect of Wei and pacification commissioner for the northern Dai frontier.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《新唐書·沙陀傳》：元和三年，盡忠款靈州塞，詔處其部鹽州置陰山府，以執宜為府兵馬使。

translations.literal: (The 《New Tang History · Shatuo Treatise》: In Yuanhe year 3 Jingzhong submitted at the Lingzhou pass; an edict settled his tribe at Yanzhou and established Yinshan Prefecture, making Zhiyi prefectural horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Tang History · Shatuo Treatise》 says: In Yuanhe 3 Jingzhong came in at Lingzhou; the court settled his people at Yanzhou as Yinshan Prefecture and made Zhiyi its horse commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朝長安，授特進、金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: He attended court at Chang'an and was given Special Advancement and general of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an he received Special Advancement and a post in the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 從攻鎮州，進蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Zhen prefecture, he was advanced to prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the Zhenzhou campaign and was promoted to Wei prefect.

sentences.zh: 破吳元濟，授檢校刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Defeating Wu Yuanji, he was made acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Yuanji was broken he received the acting post of Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，破賊深州，入朝留宿衛，拜金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Changqing he defeated bandits at Shen prefecture, entered court and remained on palace guard, and was made general of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changqing he crushed rebels at Shenzhou, stayed at court on palace guard duty, and became a Golden Crow Guard general.

sentences.zh: 太和中，授陰山府都督、代北行營招撫使。）〉

translations.literal: In Taihe he was given Yinshan Prefecture governorship and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Under Taihe he was named governor of Yinshan Prefecture and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.)〉

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡為昭烈皇帝，廟號懿祖。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Emperor Zhaolie, temple name Ancestor Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong enthroned him posthumously as Emperor Zhaolie with temple name Ancestor Yi.

sentences.zh: 烈考國昌，本名赤心，唐朔州刺史。

translations.literal: His stern father Guochang, original name Chixin, was Tang prefect of Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guochang, born Chixin, had been Tang prefect of Shuo.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，討龐勳有功，入為金吾上將軍，賜姓李氏，名國昌，

translations.literal: In Xiantong, campaigning against Pang Xun with merit, he entered court as supreme Golden Crow general, was granted the surname Li and the name Guochang,
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiantong he helped crush Pang Xun, entered court as supreme Golden Crow general, and received the imperial surname Li and the name Guochang,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （代州有《唐故龍武軍統軍檢校司徒贈太保隴四李公神道碑》云：公諱國昌，字德興。）〉

translations.literal: (At Dai prefecture there is the 《Stele of the Late Tang Longwu Army Commander-in-Chief, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi, Lord Li》 saying: the lord's taboo name was Guochang, style Dexing.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (A Dai stele, the 《Stele of Lord Li, Late Tang Longwu Commander, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi》, records his taboo name Guochang and style Dexing.)〉

sentences.zh: 仍係鄭王房。

translations.literal: and he was enrolled in the Prince of Zheng branch.
translations.idiomatic: and he was entered in the genealogical line of the Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 出為振武節度使，尋為吐渾所襲，退保於神武川。

translations.literal: He went out as Zhenwu military commissioner; soon the Tuyuhun attacked and he withdrew to hold Shenwu River.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Zhenwu military commissioner; the Tuyuhun soon struck, and he fell back to Shenwu River.

sentences.zh: 及武皇鎮太原，表為代北軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Wuhuang held Taiyuan he memorialized him as northern-campaign military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wuhuang secured Taiyuan he had him appointed military commissioner of the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 中和三年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhonghe 3.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡為文皇，廟號獻祖。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, temple name Ancestor Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong enthroned him posthumously as Emperor Wen with temple name Ancestor Xian.

sentences.zh: 武皇即獻祖之第三子也。

translations.literal: Wuhuang was Ancestor Xian's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang was the third son of Ancestor Xian.

sentences.zh: 母秦氏，以大中十年丙子歲九月二十二日，生於神武川之新城。

translations.literal: His mother was the Lady Qin; on the twenty-second day of the ninth month of the bingzi year of Dazhong 10 he was born at New City on Shenwu River.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Qin; he was born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month, bingzi year of Dazhong 10, at New City on Shenwu River.

sentences.zh: 在妊十三月，載誕之際，母艱危者竟夕。

translations.literal: She carried him thirteen months; at the moment of birth the mother was in grave peril the whole night.
translations.idiomatic: The pregnancy lasted thirteen months; on the night he was born his mother hovered between life and death.

sentences.zh: 族人憂駭，市藥於雁門，遇神叟告曰：「非巫醫所及，可馳歸，盡率部人，被甲持旄，擊鉦鼓，躍馬大噪，環所居三周而止。

translations.literal: The clansmen were alarmed and bought medicine at Yanmen; they met a divine old man who said: "This is beyond shamans and physicians—ride back at once, muster all your tribesmen in armor with banners, strike gongs and drums, gallop and shout loudly, and circle the dwelling three times, then stop.
translations.idiomatic: Kinfolk in panic sought medicine at Yanmen; a divine old man told them, "No doctor can help—gallop home, arm every tribesman with banners, beat gongs and drums, ride shouting, and circle the house three times.

sentences.zh: 」族人如其教，果無恙而生。

translations.literal: " The clansmen did as instructed and he was indeed born unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: " They did so, and mother and child came through safely.

sentences.zh: 是時，虹光燭室，白氣充庭，井水暴溢。

translations.literal: At that time a rainbow lit the chamber, white vapor filled the courtyard, and the well water suddenly overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: A rainbow filled the room, white mist flooded the courtyard, and the well burst its banks.

sentences.zh: 武皇始言，喜軍中語，齠齔善騎射，與儕類馳騁嬉戲，必出其右。

translations.literal: When Wuhuang first spoke he delighted in army talk; in childhood he excelled at riding and archery; racing and playing with his peers he always came out ahead.
translations.idiomatic: From his first words he loved camp speech; as a boy he rode and shot superbly and always beat his playmates in their games.

sentences.zh: 年十三，見雙鳧翔於空，射之連中，眾皆臣伏。

translations.literal: At thirteen he saw paired mandarin ducks flying in the sky, shot them both in succession, and all submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he brought down two mandarin ducks in one flight; onlookers bowed in awe.

sentences.zh: 新城北有毗沙天王祠，祠前井一日沸溢，武皇因持酒而奠曰：「予有尊主濟民之志，無何井溢，故未察其禍福，惟天王若有神奇，可與仆交談。

translations.literal: North of New City was a shrine to the Vaisravana Heavenly King; one day the well before the shrine boiled over; Wuhuang therefore held wine and made offering, saying: "I have the will to honor the ruler and succor the people; suddenly the well overflows, so I have not yet discerned fortune or misfortune; if the Heavenly King has divine power, you may speak with your servant.
translations.idiomatic: North of New City stood a Vaisravana shrine whose well one day boiled over; Wuhuang poured a libation and said, "I mean to serve my sovereign and save the people; this well has burst without warning, so I cannot read the omen—Heavenly King, if you have power, speak with me.

sentences.zh: 」奠酒未已，有神人被金甲持戈，隱然出於壁間，見者大驚走，惟武皇從容而退，由是益自負。

translations.literal: " Before the offering was finished a divine man in golden armor with a spear faintly emerged from the wall; those who saw it fled in terror, only Wuhuang withdrew at ease, and from this he grew still prouder.
translations.idiomatic: " Before the cup was drained an armored figure with a spear seemed to step from the wall; all fled in terror while Wuhuang walked away calmly, and his pride only grew.

sentences.zh: 獻祖之討龐勳也，武皇年十五，從征，摧鋒陷陣，出諸將之右，軍中目為「飛虎子」。

translations.literal: When Ancestor Xian campaigned against Pang Xun, Wuhuang was fifteen; he followed the expedition, smashed the van and broke formations, surpassing the generals; the army called him "Flying Tiger Cub."
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Wuhuang followed Ancestor Xian against Pang Xun, led every charge, and outshone the generals; the troops nicknamed him the Flying Tiger Cub.

sentences.zh: 賊平，獻祖授振武節度使，武皇為雲中牙將。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified Ancestor Xian was made Zhenwu military commissioner and Wuhuang became a Yunzhong adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fell Ancestor Xian received Zhenwu and Wuhuang became an adjutant at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 嘗在雲中，宿於別館，擁妓醉寢，有俠兒持刃欲害武皇；

translations.literal: Once at Yunzhong he lodged at a side hall, embraced courtesans and slept drunk; a bravo drew a blade intending to kill Wuhuang;
translations.idiomatic: Once in Yunzhong he slept drunk with courtesans in a side lodge while an assassin crept in with a blade;

sentences.zh: 及突入曲室，但見烈火熾赫於帳中，俠兒駭異而退。

translations.literal: when he burst into the inner room he saw only fierce flames blazing in the tent; the bravo fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: but inside the tent blazed with fire; the man fled in horror.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與達靼部人角勝，達靼指雙雕於空曰：「公能一發中否？

translations.literal: Again he once matched skill with men of the Tatar tribes; a Tatar pointed to paired eagles in the sky and said: "Can my lord bring them down with one shot?
translations.idiomatic: Another time he competed with Tatars who pointed to two eagles aloft and asked, "Can you drop both with one arrow?

sentences.zh: 」武皇即彎弧發矢，連貫雙雕，邊人拜伏。

translations.literal: " Wuhuang at once bent the bow and loosed; he pierced both eagles in succession and the border people bowed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: " He bent his bow and struck both; the border people prostrated themselves.

sentences.zh: 及壯，為雲中守捉使，事防禦使支謨，與同列晨集廨舍，因戲升郡閣，踞謨之座，謨亦不敢詰。

translations.literal: When grown he was Yunzhong frontier garrison commander, serving defense commissioner Zhi Mo; with his peers he gathered at dawn in the yamen and in sport climbed the prefectural tower and sat on Mo's seat; Mo also dared not reprove him.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was Yunzhong garrison commander under defense commissioner Zhi Mo; one morning he and his fellows climbed the prefectural tower for sport and sprawled on Mo's seat, and Mo did not dare rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 乾符三年，朝廷以段文楚為代北水陸發運、雲州防禦使。

translations.literal: In Qianfu year 3 the court made Duan Wenchu northern land-and-water transport commissioner and Yunzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu 3 the court appointed Duan Wenchu commissioner of northern transport and Yunzhou defense.

sentences.zh: 時歲薦饑，文楚稍削軍食，諸軍鹹怨。

translations.literal: That year famine returned; Wenchu slightly reduced army rations and all the troops resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck again; Wenchu trimmed rations and the whole army seethed.

sentences.zh: 武皇為雲中防邊督將，部下爭訴以軍食不充，邊校程懷素、王行審、蓋寓、李存璋、薛鐵山、康君立等，即擁武皇入雲州，眾且萬人，營於鬥雞台，城中械文楚出，以應於外。

translations.literal: Wuhuang was Yunzhong frontier superintendent; his men complained that rations were short; frontier officers Cheng Huaisu, Wang Xingshen, Gai Yu, Li Cunzhang, Xue Tieshan, Kang Junli, and others at once escorted Wuhuang into Yunzhou—nearly ten thousand men—encamped at Cockfight Terrace, and the city bound Wenchu and sent him out to answer them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang, as Yunzhong frontier superintendent, heard endless complaints of short rations; Cheng Huaisu, Wang Xingshen, Gai Yu, Li Cunzhang, Xue Tieshan, Kang Junli, and other frontier officers then forced him into Yunzhou with nearly ten thousand men at Cockfight Terrace while the city handed Wenchu over to them.

sentences.zh: 諸將列狀以聞，請授武皇旄鉞，朝廷不允，征諸道兵以討之。

translations.literal: The generals submitted a joint memorial asking that Wuhuang be granted the command baton; the court refused and raised troops from all circuits to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The officers memorialized jointly for Wuhuang to receive the baton of command; the court refused and mobilized every circuit against them.

sentences.zh: 乾符五年，黃巢渡江，其勢滋蔓，天子乃悟其事，以武皇為大同軍節度使、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: In Qianfu year 5 Huang Chao crossed the Yangzi and his power spread; the Son of Heaven then understood the matter and made Wuhuang Datong military commissioner and acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu 5 Huang Chao crossed the river and his strength swelled; the emperor then grasped the situation and made Wuhuang Datong military commissioner and acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 冬，獻祖出師討党項，吐渾赫連鐸乘虛陷振武，舉族為吐渾所擄。

translations.literal: Winter: Ancestor Xian marched to campaign against the Tangut; the Tuyuhun Helian Duo seized the chance and took Zhenwu; the whole clan was captured by the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Ancestor Xian marched against the Tangut; Helian Duo of the Tuyuhun struck Zhenwu in his absence and carried off the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 武皇至定邊軍迎獻祖歸雲州，雲州守將拒關不納。

translations.literal: Wuhuang went to Dingbian army to welcome Ancestor Xian back to Yunzhou; Yunzhou's garrison commander shut the pass and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang met Ancestor Xian at Dingbian and tried to return to Yunzhou, but the garrison barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 武皇略蔚、朔之地，得三千人，屯神武川之新城。

translations.literal: Wuhuang raided Wei and Shuo, gathered three thousand men, and encamped at New City on Shenwu River.
translations.idiomatic: He swept Wei and Shuo, raised three thousand men, and camped at New City on Shenwu River.

sentences.zh: 赫邊鐸晝夜攻圍，武皇昆弟三人四面應賊，俄而獻祖自蔚州引軍至，吐渾退走，自是軍勢復振。

translations.literal: Helian Duo besieged day and night; Wuhuang and his three brothers answered the enemy on four sides; presently Ancestor Xian led troops from Wei prefecture; the Tuyuhun withdrew, and from this the army's strength revived.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo pressed the siege without pause; Wuhuang and his three brothers fought on every side until Ancestor Xian marched from Weizhou and the Tuyuhun pulled back; their power revived.

sentences.zh: 天子以赫連鐸為大同軍節度使，仍命進軍以討武皇。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven made Helian Duo Datong military commissioner and still ordered advance to campaign against Wuhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Helian Duo Datong commissioner and ordered him to march on Wuhuang.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年春，朝廷以昭義節度使李鈞充北面招討使，將上黨、太原之師過石嶺關，屯於代州，與幽州李可舉會赫連鐸同攻蔚州。

translations.literal: Spring of Qianfu year 6: the court made Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Jun northern campaign commander-in-chief, leading Shangdang and Taiyuan troops through Shiling Pass to encamp at Dai prefecture, and with Youzhou's Li Keju joined Helian Duo to attack Weizhou together.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Qianfu 6 Li Jun of Zhaoyi was made northern commander-in-chief; he led Shangdang and Taiyuan forces through Shiling Pass to Dai, and with Li Keju of Youzhou and Helian Duo besieged Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 獻祖以一軍禦之，武皇以一軍南抵遮虜城以拒李鈞。

translations.literal: Ancestor Xian held them with one army; Wuhuang with one army went south to Zhelu Fort to block Li Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Xian met them with one wing; Wuhuang took another south to Zhelu Fort to stop Li Jun.

sentences.zh: 是冬大雪，弓弩弦折，南軍苦寒，臨戰大敗，奔歸代州，李鈞中流矢而卒。

translations.literal: That winter heavy snow snapped bowstrings; the southern army suffered bitter cold, was utterly defeated in battle, fled back to Dai, and Li Jun died of an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow that winter snapped every bowstring; the southern force froze, broke in battle, fled to Dai, and Li Jun died of an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年春，天子復命元帥李涿率兵數萬屯代州。

translations.literal: Spring of Guangming year 1: the Son of Heaven again ordered marshal Li Zhuo to lead tens of thousands of troops to encamp at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Guangming 1 the emperor again sent Marshal Li Zhuo with tens of thousands to camp at Dai.

sentences.zh: 武皇令軍使傅文達起兵於蔚州，朔州刺史高文集與薛葛、安慶等部將縛文達送於李涿。

translations.literal: Wuhuang ordered army commissioner Fu Wenda to raise troops at Weizhou; Shuo prefect Gao Wenji with subordinates Xue Ge, An Qing, and others bound Wenda and sent him to Li Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang had Fu Wenda raise troops at Weizhou; Shuo prefect Gao Wenji and officers Xue Ge and An Qing bound Wenda and delivered him to Li Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 六月，李涿引大軍攻蔚州，獻祖戰不利，乃率其族奔於達靼部。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Li Zhuo led a great army to attack Weizhou; Ancestor Xian fought unfavorably and then led his clan in flight to the Tatar tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Zhuo assaulted Weizhou; Ancestor Xian was beaten and fled with his clan to the Tatars.

sentences.zh: 居數月，吐渾赫連鐸密遣人賂達靼以離間獻祖，既而漸生猜阻。

translations.literal: After several months the Tuyuhun Helian Duo secretly sent men to bribe the Tatars to estrange Ancestor Xian, and suspicion gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Helian Duo bribed the Tatars to turn against Ancestor Xian, and distrust slowly took hold.

sentences.zh: 武皇知之，每召其豪右射獵於野，或與之百步馳射馬鞭，或以懸針樹葉為的，中之如神，由是部人心伏，不敢竊發。

translations.literal: Wuhuang knew it; he often summoned their chieftains to hunt in the wild, or raced them at a hundred paces shooting at horsewhips, or used hanging needles and tree leaves as targets and hit them like a spirit; thereby the tribes submitted in heart and dared not act secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang saw it; he hunted with their leaders, matched them shooting horsewhips at a hundred paces, or pinned hanging needles and leaves—and never missed; the tribes submitted in awe and dared not plot.

sentences.zh: 俄而黃巢自江、淮北渡，武皇椎牛釃酒，饗其酋首。

translations.literal: Presently Huang Chao crossed north from south of the Yangzi and Huai; Wuhuang slaughtered oxen and poured wine to feast their chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao crossed the Huai from the south, Wuhuang feasted the Tatar chiefs with oxen and wine.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，諭之曰：「予父子為賊臣讒間，報國無由。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep he admonished them, saying: "My father and I were estranged by slanderous ministers and had no way to serve the state.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in his cups he told them, "Slander cut my father and me off from the throne—we could not serve the realm.

sentences.zh: 今聞黃巢北犯江、淮，必為中原之患。

translations.literal: Now I hear Huang Chao is marching north against the Yangzi and Huai and will surely become a scourge to the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: Now Huang Chao drives north along the Yangzi and Huai and will ravage the heartland.

sentences.zh: 一日天子赦宥，有詔征兵，仆與公等向南而定天下，是予心也。

translations.literal: If one day the Son of Heaven pardons and an edict summons troops, your servant with you will march south and settle the realm—that is my heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor pardons us and calls for armies, I mean to march south with you and settle the empire.

sentences.zh: 人生世間，光景幾何，曷能終老沙堆中哉！

translations.literal: How long is a man's life in this world—how can we end our days in desert sands!
translations.idiomatic: Life is brief—who wants to die in the sand?

sentences.zh: 公等勉之。

translations.literal: Do your best, gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Take heart, all of you.

sentences.zh: 」達靼知無留意，皆釋然無間。

translations.literal: " The Tatars knew he had no mind to stay and all relaxed without estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: " Seeing he would not linger, the Tatars put aside suspicion.

sentences.zh: 是歲十一月，黃巢寇潼關，天子令河東監軍陳景思為代北起軍使，收兵破賊。

translations.literal: That year, eleventh month: Huang Chao threatened Tong Pass; the Son of Heaven ordered Hedong eunuch commissioner Chen Jingsi northern recruiting commissioner to gather troops and break the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Huang Chao threatened Tong Pass; the emperor made Chen Jingsi of Hedong northern recruiting commissioner to raise troops against him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，黃巢犯長安，僖宗幸蜀，陳景思與李友金發沙陁諸部五千騎南赴京師。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Huang Chao entered Chang'an; Emperor Xizong fled to Shu; Chen Jingsi and Li Youjin led five thousand Shatuo cavalry south toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Huang Chao took Chang'an; Xizong fled to Shu; Chen Jingsi and Li Youjin led five thousand Shatuo horsemen south to the capital.

sentences.zh: 友金即武皇之族父也。

translations.literal: Youjin was Wuhuang's clansman uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Youjin was Wuhuang's kinsman on his father's side.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：友金初與高文集並降於李琢，故得與陳景思南赴京師。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》: Youjin had first surrendered with Gao Wenji to Li Zhuo, and therefore could march south with Chen Jingsi.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Youjin had surrendered with Gao Wenji to Li Zhuo, which let him join Chen Jingsi's march south.)〉

sentences.zh: 中和元年二月，友金軍至絳州，將渡河，刺史瞿稹謂陳景思曰：「巢賊方盛，不如且還代北，徐圖利害。

translations.literal: Second month, Zhonghe year 1: Youjin's army reached Jiang prefecture and was about to cross the river; prefect Qu Zhi said to Chen Jingsi: "The Chao bandits are still strong; better for now to return to Dai and weigh advantage slowly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhonghe 1 Youjin reached Jiangzhou to cross the river; Qu Zhi told Chen Jingsi, "Chao is still rampant—fall back to Dai for now and choose your moment.

sentences.zh: 」四月，友金旋軍雁門，瞿稹至代州，半月之間，募兵三萬，營於崞縣之西。

translations.literal: " Fourth month: Youjin turned the army to Yanmen; Qu Zhi reached Dai prefecture; within half a month he recruited thirty thousand troops and encamped west of Guo county.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month Youjin withdrew to Yanmen; Qu Zhi reached Dai and raised thirty thousand men west of Guo in a fortnight.

sentences.zh: 其軍皆北邊五部之眾，不閑軍法，瞿正、李友金不能制。

translations.literal: The army was all men of the five northern tribes, unskilled in military law; Qu Zheng and Li Youjin could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: They were tribesmen of the five northern confederacies, untrained in drill; neither Qu Zheng nor Li Youjin could hold them.

sentences.zh: 友金謂景思曰：「興大眾，成大事，當威名素著，則可以伏人。

translations.literal: Youjin said to Jingsi: "To raise a great host and accomplish a great deed one must already possess renown, then one can overawe men.
translations.idiomatic: Youjin told Jingsi, "A great host needs a name men already fear.

sentences.zh: 今軍雖數萬，苟無善帥，進亦無功。

translations.literal: Now though the army numbers tens of thousands, without a good commander advance will also be fruitless.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands without a proven leader will march nowhere.

sentences.zh: 吾兄李司徒父子，去歲獲罪於國家，今寄北部，雄武之略，為眾所推。

translations.literal: My elder brother Minister Li and his son last year offended the state and now lodge in the north; their bold strategy is what the masses push forward.
translations.idiomatic: My kinsman Minister Li and his son offended the court last year and shelter in the north; everyone trusts their martial genius.

sentences.zh: 若驃騎急奏召還，代北之人，一麾響應，則妖賊不足平也。

translations.literal: If the commissioner urgently memorializes to recall them, the men of Dai will answer at one wave of the banner, and the demon bandits will not be hard to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Summon them by urgent memorial and every northerner will rally—Chao will fall easily.

sentences.zh: 」景思然之，促奏行在。

translations.literal: " Jingsi agreed and hurried a memorial to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingsi agreed and rushed word to the court in exile.

sentences.zh: 天子乃以武皇為雁門節度使，仍令以本軍討賊。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven then made Wuhuang Yanmen military commissioner and still ordered his army to campaign against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then named Wuhuang Yanmen military commissioner and ordered his troops against the rebels.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《新唐書·王重榮傳》：重榮懼黃巢復振，憂之，與復光計，復光曰：「我世與李克用共憂患，其人忠不顧難，死義如己，若乞師焉，事蔑不濟。

translations.literal: (The 《New Tang History · Wang Chongrong Biography》: Chongrong feared Huang Chao would revive and was anxious; with Fuguang he took counsel; Fuguang said: "My house and Li Keyong have shared hardship for generations; the man is loyal and heedless of danger, treats death as his own—if you beg troops of him, nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Tang History · Wang Chongrong Biography》 says Chongrong dreaded Chao's return and consulted Fuguang, who said, "Our houses and Li Keyong have shared peril for generations; he is loyal, fearless, and treats another's death as his own—ask him for troops and you cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使者約連和。）〉

translations.literal: " He then sent envoys to arrange alliance.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Envoys were sent to ally with him.)〉

sentences.zh: 李友金發五百騎齎詔召武皇於達靼，武皇即率達靼諸部萬人趨雁門。

translations.literal: Li Youjin sent five hundred cavalry bearing the edict to summon Wuhuang from the Tatars; Wuhuang at once led ten thousand men of the Tatar tribes toward Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Youjin sent five hundred horsemen with the edict to fetch Wuhuang from the Tatars; he led ten thousand Tatar riders straight for Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 五月，整兵二萬，南向京師。

translations.literal: Fifth month: he mustered twenty thousand troops and marched south toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he gathered twenty thousand men and marched south on the capital.

sentences.zh: 太原鄭從讜以兵守石嶺關，武皇乃引軍出他道；

translations.literal: Taiyuan's Zheng Congdian held troops at Shiling Pass; Wuhuang therefore led the army by another route;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Congdian of Taiyuan blocked Shiling Pass; Wuhuang detoured;

sentences.zh: 至太原城下，會大雨，班師於雁門。

translations.literal: reaching below Taiyuan city he met great rain and withdrew the army to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: but heavy rain at Taiyuan forced him back to Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 中和二年八月，獻祖自達靼部率其族歸代州。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Zhonghe year 2: Ancestor Xian led his clan back from the Tatar tribes to Dai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhonghe 2 Ancestor Xian brought his clan home from the Tatars to Dai.

sentences.zh: 十月，武皇率忻、代、蔚、朔、達靼之軍三萬五千騎赴難於京師。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Wuhuang led thirty-five thousand cavalry of Xin, Dai, Wei, Shuo, and the Tatars south to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wuhuang marched south with thirty-five thousand horse from Xin, Dai, Wei, Shuo, and the Tatars to save the court.

sentences.zh: 先移檄太原，鄭從讜拒關不納，武皇以兵擊之，進軍至城下，遣人齎幣馬遺從讜；

translations.literal: First he sent a proclamation to Taiyuan; Zheng Congdian shut the pass and would not admit them; Wuhuang attacked with troops, advanced to below the wall, and sent men bearing gifts of silks and horses to Congdian;
translations.idiomatic: He announced his coming at Taiyuan; Congdian barred the pass; Wuhuang assaulted the city and sent gifts of silk and horses;

sentences.zh: 從讜亦遣人饋武皇貨幣、饔餼、軍器。

translations.literal: Congdian also sent men presenting Wuhuang with goods, provisions, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Congdian replied with goods, food, and arms.

sentences.zh: 武皇南去，自陰地趨晉、絳。

translations.literal: Wuhuang went south by the Yindi route toward Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang turned south through Yindi toward Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，武皇至河中。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Wuhuang reached Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he reached Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 中和三年正月，晉國公王鐸承製授武皇東北面行營都統。

translations.literal: First month, Zhonghe year 3: Jin State Duke Wang Duo, by imperial order, made Wuhuang overall commander of the northeastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhonghe 3 Wang Duo, Duke of Jin, appointed Wuhuang overall commander of the northeastern campaign by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 武皇令其弟克修領前鋒五百騎渡河視賊，黃巢遣將米重威齎重賂及偽詔以賜武皇；

translations.literal: Wuhuang ordered his younger brother Kexiu to lead five hundred vanguard cavalry across the river to reconnoiter the bandits; Huang Chao sent the general Mi Chongwei bearing heavy bribes and a false edict to bestow on Wuhuang;
translations.idiomatic: He sent his brother Kexiu with five hundred vanguard horsemen to scout the rebels; Chao's general Mi Chongwei came with rich gifts and a forged edict;

sentences.zh: 武皇納其賂以給諸將，燔其偽詔。

translations.literal: Wuhuang took the bribes to supply the generals and burned the false edict.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang paid his officers from the bribes and burned the forged edict.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸道勤王之師雲集京畿，然以賊勢尚熾，未敢爭鋒。

translations.literal: At that time the relief armies of all circuits gathered thickly about the capital, yet because the bandit power was still fierce none dared contend at the spearpoint.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit had sent relief troops to the capital, but Chao was still too strong for anyone to close with him.

sentences.zh: 及武皇將至，賊帥相謂曰：「鴉兒軍至，當避其鋒。

translations.literal: When Wuhuang was about to arrive, the bandit chiefs said to one another: "The Crow-Son Army is coming—we must avoid their edge.
translations.idiomatic: As Wuhuang drew near, the rebel commanders said among themselves: "The Crow-Son Army is here—we must give way to their attack.

sentences.zh: 」武皇以兵自夏陽濟河。

translations.literal: " Wuhuang led his troops across the river from Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuhuang crossed the Yellow River from Xiayang with his army.

sentences.zh: 二月，營於乾坑店。

translations.literal: Second month, he encamped at Qiangeng Post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he camped at Qiangeng Post.

sentences.zh: 黃巢大將尚讓、林言、王璠、趙璋等引軍十五萬屯於梁田坡。

translations.literal: Huang Chao's great generals Shang Rang, Lin Yan, Wang Fan, and Zhao Zhang led a hundred and fifty thousand men and encamped at Liangtian Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang, Lin Yan, Wang Fan, and Zhao Zhang, Huang Chao's chief generals, brought a hundred and fifty thousand men to Liangtian Slope.

sentences.zh: 翌日，大軍合戰，自午及晡，巢賊大敗。

translations.literal: The next day the armies joined battle; from noon until the second watch the Chao bandits were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the armies fought from noon until dusk and Huang Chao's forces were routed.

sentences.zh: 是夜，賊眾遁據華州。

translations.literal: That night the bandit host fled and held Hua prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rebels withdrew into Hua prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武皇進軍圍之，巢弟黃鄴、黃揆固守。

translations.literal: Wuhuang advanced to besiege it; Huang Chao's younger brothers Huang Ye and Huang Kui held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang pressed the siege while Huang Ye and Huang Kui, Huang Chao's brothers, defended the city.

sentences.zh: 三月，尚讓引大軍赴援，武皇率兵萬餘逆戰於零口，巢軍大敗，武皇進軍渭橋。

translations.literal: Third month, Shang Rang led a great army to the relief; Wuhuang with more than ten thousand men met them in battle at Lingkou, the Chao army was crushed, and Wuhuang marched to Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Shang Rang marched to relieve the city; Wuhuang met him at Lingkou with over ten thousand men, routed the Chao army, and advanced to Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 翌日，黃揆棄華州而遁。

translations.literal: The next day Huang Kui abandoned Hua prefecture and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Huang Kui abandoned Hua and fled.

sentences.zh: 王鐸承製授武皇雁門節度使、檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Wang Duo, acting on imperial commission, appointed Wuhuang military commissioner of Yanmen and honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo, acting on imperial orders, made Wuhuang military commissioner of Yanmen and honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四月，黃巢燔長安，收其餘眾，東走藍關。

translations.literal: Fourth month, Huang Chao burned Chang'an, gathered his remaining followers, and fled east through Lan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Huang Chao burned Chang'an, rallied his survivors, and fled east through Lan Pass.

sentences.zh: 武皇時收京師。

translations.literal: Wuhuang was then recovering the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang was then taking control of the capital.

sentences.zh: 七月，天子授武皇金紫光祿大夫、檢校左僕射、河東節度使。

translations.literal: Seventh month, the Son of Heaven appointed Wuhuang Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, honorary Left Vice Director, and military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor named Wuhuang Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, honorary Left Vice Director, and military commissioner of Hedong.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《舊唐書·僖宗紀》：五月，製以雁門以北行營節度、忻代蔚朔等州觀察處置等使、檢校尚書左僕射、代州刺史、上柱國、食邑七百戶李克用檢校司空、同平章事兼太原尹、北京留守，充河東節度、管內觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang · Annals of Emperor Xizong》 says: In the fifth month, by imperial edict, Li Keyong, campaign commissioner north of Yanmen, observation and disposition commissioner for Xin, Dai, Wei, Shuo, and other prefectures, honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, prefect of Dai, Supreme Pillar of State, with a fief of seven hundred households, was made honorary Minister of Works, Tongping Grand Councilor, concurrently Grand Governor of Taiyuan and Beijing Protector, and military commissioner of Hedong with full authority over his circuit.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Old Book of Tang · Annals of Emperor Xizong》 records that in the fifth month Li Keyong—already campaign commissioner north of Yanmen and military commissioner of Xin, Dai, Wei, and Shuo—was promoted to Minister of Works, Tongping Grand Councilor, Grand Governor of Taiyuan, and full Hedong commissioner.)

sentences.zh: 《新唐書·沙陀傳》云：收京師功第一，進同中書門下平章事、隴西郡公。

translations.literal: The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of the Shatuo》 says: For first merit in recovering the capital he was advanced to Tongzhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi and Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of the Shatuo》 adds that for leading the recovery of the capital he became Tongping Grand Councilor and Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以克用領河東節度。）〉

translations.literal: Before long Li Keyong was put in charge of the Hedong commission.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he took up the Hedong commission in full.)〉

sentences.zh: 是時，武皇既收長安，軍勢甚雄，諸侯之師皆畏之。

translations.literal: At that time Wuhuang had recovered Chang'an and his army was very strong; the armies of the other lords all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wuhuang held Chang'an and his army was so powerful that the other warlords feared him.

sentences.zh: 武皇一目微眇，故其時號為「獨眼龍」。

translations.literal: Wuhuang had one eye slightly blind, and for that reason he was then called the "One-Eyed Dragon."
translations.idiomatic: One of his eyes was weak, and men called him the "One-Eyed Dragon."

sentences.zh: 是月，武皇仗節赴鎮。

translations.literal: That month Wuhuang went to his commission bearing the imperial baton.
translations.idiomatic: That month he set out for his post with the imperial baton of office.

sentences.zh: 遣使報鄭從讜，請治裝歸朝。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to inform Zheng Congdang and asked him to prepare to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: He notified Zheng Congdang and asked him to make ready for the return to court.

sentences.zh: 武皇次於郊外，因往赴雁門寧覲獻祖。

translations.literal: Wuhuang halted in the suburbs and then went to Yanmen to pay a reverent visit to his ancestor Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He paused in the suburbs, then went to Yanmen to pay his respects at the tomb of his ancestor Xian.

sentences.zh: 八月，自雁門赴鎮河東，時年二十有八。

translations.literal: Eighth month, he left Yanmen for his Hedong commission; he was twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he left Yanmen for Hedong; he was twenty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 十一月，平潞州，表其弟克修為昭義節度使。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, he pacified Lu prefecture and memorialized that his younger brother Kexiu be made military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he took Lu prefecture and asked that his brother Kexiu be made Zhaoyi military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 潞帥孟方立退保於邢州。

translations.literal: The Lu commander Meng Fangli withdrew to hold Xing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Fangli, the Lu commander, fell back to defend Xing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二月，許帥田從異、汴帥朱溫、徐帥時溥、陳州刺史趙犨各遣使來告，以巢、蔡合從，凶鋒尚熾，請武皇共力討賊。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Tian Congyi of Xu prefecture, Zhu Wen of Bian, Shi Pu of Xuzhou, and Zhao Chou, prefect of Chen, each sent envoys to report that Huang Chao and Cai had joined forces, their ferocity was still fierce, and to ask Wuhuang to join in exterminating the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Tian Congyi of Xu prefecture, Zhu Wen of Bian, Shi Pu of Xuzhou, and Zhao Chou of Chen each wrote that Huang Chao and the Cai rebels were allied and still dangerous, and begged Wuhuang to help destroy them.

sentences.zh: 中和四年春，武皇率蕃漢之師五萬，自澤、潞將下天井關；

translations.literal: Spring of the fourth year of Zhonghe, Wuhuang led fifty thousand Tartar and Chinese troops from Ze and Lu toward Tianjing Pass;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Zhonghe 4 Wuhuang led fifty thousand mixed Tartar and Chinese troops from Ze and Lu down on Tianjing Pass;

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使諸葛爽辭以河橋不完，乃屯兵於萬善。

translations.literal: the Hedong commissioner Zhuge Shuang pleaded that the Yellow River bridge was not complete, so the army encamped at Wanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Shuang of Heyang said the river bridge was unfinished, so the army halted at Wanshan.

sentences.zh: 數日。

translations.literal: Several days passed.
translations.idiomatic: After several days,

sentences.zh: 移軍自河中南渡，趨汝、洛。

translations.literal: he shifted the army, crossed south from Heyang, and pressed toward Ru and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: he crossed the river from Heyang and marched on Ru and Luo.

sentences.zh: 四月，武皇合徐、汴之師破尚讓於太康，斬獲萬計，進攻賊於西華，賊將黃鄴棄營而遁。

translations.literal: Fourth month, Wuhuang combined with the Xu and Bian armies to defeat Shang Rang at Taikang, beheading and capturing tens of thousands, then attacked the bandits at Xihua; the bandit general Huang Ye abandoned camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, with the Xu and Bian armies, he crushed Shang Rang at Taikang, took tens of thousands of heads and captives, and drove on Xihua until Huang Ye abandoned his camp.

sentences.zh: 是夜大雨，巢營中驚亂，乃棄西華之壘，退營陳州北故陽裏。

translations.literal: That night a great rain fell; Chao's camp was thrown into alarm, and they abandoned the Xihua fort and withdrew to the old Yang quarter north of Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That night heavy rain panicked Huang Chao's camp; they left Xihua and fell back to the old Yang quarter north of Chen.

sentences.zh: 五月癸亥，大雨震電，平地水深數尺，賊營為水所漂而潰。

translations.literal: On guihai of the fifth month, great rain, thunder, and lightning; the water on level ground was several feet deep, and the bandit camps were washed away and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai in the fifth month thunder and torrential rain flooded the plain several feet deep and washed the rebel camps away.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，武皇引軍營於中牟，大破賊於王滿渡。

translations.literal: On wuchen Wuhuang led the army to camp at Zhongmou and inflicted a great defeat on the bandits at Wangman Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he encamped at Zhongmou and routed the rebels at Wangman Ford.

sentences.zh: 庚午，巢賊大至，濟汴而北。

translations.literal: On gengwu the Chao bandits came in force and crossed the Bian River going north.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Huang Chao brought up his main force and crossed the Bian River northward.

sentences.zh: 是夜，復大雨，賊黨驚潰。

translations.literal: That night there was again great rain, and the bandit party panicked and broke.
translations.idiomatic: That night another storm broke the rebel ranks in panic.

sentences.zh: 武皇營於鄭州，賊眾分寇汴境。

translations.literal: Wuhuang encamped at Zhengzhou; the bandit host split to raid the Bian frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang camped at Zhengzhou while rebel detachments raided the Bian border.

sentences.zh: 武皇渡汴，遇賊將渡而南，半濟擊之，大敗之，臨陣斬賊將李周、王濟安、陽景彪等。

translations.literal: Wuhuang crossed the Bian, met bandit generals crossing south, struck them halfway across, routed them utterly, and on the field beheaded the bandit generals Li Zhou, Wang Ji'an, and Yang Jingbiao.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Bian, caught rebel columns mid-river, cut them down, and killed Li Zhou, Wang Ji'an, and Yang Jingbiao in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 是夜，賊大敗，殘眾保於胙縣、冤句。

translations.literal: That night the bandits were crushed; the survivors held Zuo county and Yuanqu.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rebels were shattered; the remnants held Zuo county and Yuanqu.

sentences.zh: 大軍躡之，黃巢乃攜妻子兄弟千餘人東走，武皇追賊至於曹州。

translations.literal: The main army pressed them; Huang Chao then took his wife, children, and brothers—a thousand and more—and fled east; Wuhuang pursued the bandits to Cao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit closed in; Huang Chao fled east with more than a thousand kin; Wuhuang chased him as far as Cao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是月，班師過汴，汴帥迎勞於封禪寺，請武皇休於府第，乃以從官三百人及監軍使陳景思館於上源驛。

translations.literal: That month, on the return march he passed Bian; the Bian commander welcomed and feasted him at Fengchan Temple and asked Wuhuang to rest at his mansion, lodging his three hundred followers and the army supervisor Chen Jingsi at Shangyuan Post.
translations.idiomatic: On the homeward march that month he stopped at Bian; the Bian commander entertained him at Fengchan Temple and invited him to his residence while three hundred staff and the supervisor Chen Jingsi were lodged at Shangyuan Post.

sentences.zh: 是夜，張樂陳宴席，汴帥自佐饗，出珍幣侑勸。

translations.literal: That night music was arranged and a banquet set out; the Bian commander himself attended the feast and produced rare gifts to urge toasts.
translations.idiomatic: That night there was a banquet with music; the Bian commander waited on him in person and offered costly gifts with the wine.

sentences.zh: 武皇酒酣，戲諸侍妓，與汴帥握手，敘破賊事以為樂。

translations.literal: Wuhuang, flushed with wine, jested with the attendant women, clasped the Bian commander's hand, and took pleasure in recounting how they had broken the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Wuhuang bantered with the singing girls, clasped the Bian commander's hand, and exulted over their victory over the rebels.

sentences.zh: 汴帥素忌武皇，乃與其將楊彥洪密謀竊發，彥洪於巷陌連車樹柵，以扼奔竄之路。

translations.literal: The Bian commander had long resented Wuhuang; he and his general Yang Yanhong secretly plotted a surprise attack, and Yanhong lined carts in the lanes and set barriers to block escape.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian commander had long envied him; he and Yang Yanhong plotted a night attack and barricaded the streets with chained carts.

sentences.zh: 時武皇之從官皆醉，俄而伏兵竄發，來攻傳舍。

translations.literal: At the time Wuhuang's attendants were all drunk; suddenly hidden troops burst forth and attacked the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang's party was drunk when ambushers stormed the lodge.

sentences.zh: 武皇方大醉，噪聲動地，從官十餘人捍賊。

translations.literal: Wuhuang was deep in wine; the uproar shook the earth, and a dozen or so attendants fought the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Still heavily drunk, he heard the clamor; a dozen followers fought off the attackers.

sentences.zh: 侍人郭景銖滅燭扶武皇，以茵幕裹之，匿於床下，以水灑麵，徐曰：「汴帥謀害司空！

translations.literal: The attendant Guo Jingyin extinguished the lamps, supported Wuhuang, wrapped him in a curtain, hid him under the bed, sprinkled water on his face, and said slowly: "The Bian commander plots to kill the Minister of Works!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jingyin put out the lamps, steadied Wuhuang, wrapped him in bedding, hid him beneath the couch, splashed water on his face, and whispered: "The Bian commander means to murder you, Minister of Works!

sentences.zh: 」武皇方張目而起，引弓抗賊。

translations.literal: " Wuhuang then opened his eyes, rose, and drew his bow against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " He opened his eyes, got up, and shot back at the assailants.

sentences.zh: 有頃，煙火四合，復大雨震電，武皇得從者薛鐵山、賀回鶻等數人而去。

translations.literal: Before long fire blazed on every side; again great rain, thunder, and lightning; Wuhuang escaped with several followers including Xue Tieshan and He Huihu.
translations.idiomatic: Fire closed in on every side; thunder and rain broke again; he escaped with Xue Tieshan, He Huihu, and a few others.

sentences.zh: 雨水如澍，不辨人物，隨電光登尉氏門，縋城而出，得還本營。

translations.literal: The rain poured like a flood; men could not be told apart; by lightning he climbed Weishi Gate, was lowered from the wall by rope, and returned to his own camp.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell in sheets and men could not see one another; by a flash of lightning he scaled Weishi Gate, was let down by rope, and reached his camp.

sentences.zh: 監軍陳景思、大將史敬思並遇害。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Chen Jingsi and the great general Shi Jingsi were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingsi, the army supervisor, and the general Shi Jingsi were killed.

sentences.zh: 武皇既還營，與劉夫人相向慟哭。

translations.literal: Once Wuhuang was back in camp, he and Lady Liu wept face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Back in camp he and Lady Liu wept together.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，欲勒軍攻汴，夫人曰：「司空比為國家討賊，赴東諸侯之急，雖汴人謀害，自有朝廷論列。

translations.literal: At dawn he wished to marshal the army against Bian; the lady said: "The Minister of Works has lately served the state in exterminating bandits and rushed east to relieve the other lords; though the men of Bian plotted against you, the court itself will judge the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he wanted to turn the army on Bian; Lady Liu said: "You have just served the throne against the rebels and hurried east at the other lords' call; if Bian plotted against you, the court will judge it.

sentences.zh: 若反戈攻城，則曲在我也，人得以為辭。

translations.literal: If you turn your blades to storm a city, the wrong will be on our side, and others will have grounds to speak against you.
translations.idiomatic: If you attack their city, the fault will be yours and they will have a case against you.

sentences.zh: 」乃收軍而去，馳檄於汴帥。

translations.literal: " He then withdrew the army and sent a rapid dispatch to the Bian commander.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew off the army and sent an urgent message to the Bian commander.

sentences.zh: 汴帥報曰：「竊發之夜，非仆本心，是朝廷遣天使與牙將楊彥洪同謀也。

translations.literal: The Bian commander replied: "On the night of the surprise attack it was not my own intent; the court sent an imperial envoy who plotted together with the military commissioner Yang Yanhong."
translations.idiomatic: The Bian commander answered: "I did not intend that night's attack; an imperial envoy from the court plotted it with Yang Yanhong."

sentences.zh: 」武皇自武牢關西趨蒲、陝而旋。

translations.literal: Wuhuang went west through Wulao Pass toward Pu and Shan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang marched west through Wulao Pass by way of Pu and Shan and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，至太原。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, he reached Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he reached Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 武皇自以累立大功，為汴帥怨圖，陷沒諸將，乃上章申理。

translations.literal: Wuhuang, considering that he had repeatedly achieved great merit yet been plotted against by the Bian commander with the loss of many generals, submitted a memorial to state his case.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling that his repeated victories had been repaid with the Bian commander's treachery and the death of his officers, he memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 及武皇表至，朝廷大恐，遣內臣宣諭，尋加守太傅、同平章事、隴西郡王。

translations.literal: When Wuhuang's memorial arrived the court was greatly alarmed, sent an inner courtier to soothe him with edicts, and soon added Grand Tutor, Tongping Grand Councilor, and Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: The court was alarmed when his memorial arrived, sent an inner envoy to reassure him, and soon made him Grand Tutor, Tongping Grand Councilor, and Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，河中王重榮遣使來乞師，且言邠州朱玫、鳳翔李符將加兵於己。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Wang Chongrong of Hezhong sent envoys begging for troops and reporting that Zhu Mei of Bin and Li Fu of Fengxiang were about to add troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wang Chongrong of Hezhong asked for aid, saying Zhu Mei of Bin and Li Fu of Fengxiang were marching against him.

sentences.zh: 初，武皇與汴人構怨，前後八表，請削奪汴帥官爵，自以本軍進討。

translations.literal: Earlier, because of his feud with the men of Bian, Wuhuang had eight times memorialized asking that the Bian commander's titles be stripped and that he himself lead his army in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Already bitter toward Bian, Wuhuang had eight times asked that Zhu Wen be degraded and that he be allowed to attack him.

sentences.zh: 天子累遣內臣楊復恭宣旨，令且全大體，武皇不時奉詔，天子頗右汴帥。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven repeatedly sent the inner courtier Yang Fugong to announce edicts telling him to preserve the larger settlement; Wuhuang did not promptly obey, and the Son of Heaven rather favored the Bian commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent Yang Fugong to urge restraint; Wuhuang delayed obeying, and the court leaned toward Bian.

sentences.zh: 時觀軍容使田令孜君側擅權，惡王重榮與武皇膠固，將離其勢，乃移重榮於定州。

translations.literal: At the time the army supervisor Tian Lingzi wielded power at the ruler's side, hated the close bond between Wang Chongrong and Wuhuang, and wished to break their strength, so he transferred Chongrong to Ding prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi, the army supervisor, hated the alliance of Chongrong and Wuhuang and tried to split them by moving Chongrong to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 重榮告於武皇，武皇上章言：「李符、朱玫挾邪忌正，黨庇朱溫。

translations.literal: Chongrong informed Wuhuang; Wuhuang memorialized: "Li Fu and Zhu Mei harbor evil, hate the upright, and shield Zhu Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong appealed to Wuhuang, who wrote: "Li Fu and Zhu Mei are corrupt, hate the loyal, and protect Zhu Wen.

sentences.zh: 臣已點檢蕃漢軍五萬，取來年渡河，先斬朱玫、李冒符，然後平蕩朱溫。」

translations.literal: Your subject has mustered fifty thousand Tartar and Chinese troops and will cross the river next year, first behead Zhu Mei and Li Mao-fu, and then sweep away Zhu Wen."
translations.idiomatic: I have fifty thousand Tartar and Chinese troops ready and will cross the river next year, kill Zhu Mei and Li Fu, and then destroy Zhu Wen."

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《新唐書·王重榮傳》：詔克用將兵援河中，重榮貽克用書，且言：「奉密詔，須公到，使我圖公，此令孜、朱全忠、朱玫之惑上也。

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of Wang Chongrong》 says: An edict ordered Li Keyong to lead troops to aid Hezhong; Chongrong sent Keyong a letter saying: "I have received a secret edict that, once you arrive, I am to plot against you—this is the deception of Lingzi, Zhu Quanzhong, and Zhu Mei at the court's ear."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of Wang Chongrong》 says: When Li Keyong was ordered to aid Hezhong, Chongrong wrote that a secret edict required him to destroy Keyong once he came—that Tian Lingzi, Zhu Quanzhong, and Zhu Mei had misled the throne.)

sentences.zh: 」因示偽詔。

translations.literal: He then showed the forged edict.
translations.idiomatic: He showed the forged edict as proof.

sentences.zh: 克用方與全忠有隙，信之，請討全忠及玫。）〉

translations.literal: Keyong was then at odds with Quanzhong, believed it, and asked permission to attack Quanzhong and Mei.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Keyong, already hostile to Zhu Quanzhong, believed him and asked to attack Quanzhong and Mei.)〉

sentences.zh: 天子覽表，遣使譬喻百端，軺傳相望。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven read the memorial and sent envoys to explain in a hundred ways; relay-chariots followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and sent envoy after envoy to reason with him; dispatches crowded the road.

sentences.zh: 既而朱玫引邠、鳳之師攻河中，王重榮出師拒戰。

translations.literal: Before long Zhu Mei led the Bin and Fengxiang armies against Hezhong; Wang Chongrong marched out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu Mei brought the Bin and Fengxiang armies against Hezhong and Chongrong marched out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 朱玫軍於沙苑，對壘月餘。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei's army encamped at Shayuan; the two sides faced each other for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei camped at Shayuan and the armies faced each other for over a month.

sentences.zh: 十二月，武皇引軍渡河，與朱玫決戰，玫大敗，收軍夜遁，入於京師。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Wuhuang led troops across the river, fought Zhu Mei to the decision, Mei was utterly defeated, drew off the army and fled by night, and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wuhuang crossed the river, routed Zhu Mei in a decisive battle, and Mei fled by night into the capital.

sentences.zh: 時京城大駭。

translations.literal: At the time the capital was in great alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 天子幸鳳翔，武皇退軍於河中。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven fled to Fengxiang; Wuhuang withdrew the army to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to Fengxiang; Wuhuang pulled back to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年正月，僖宗駐蹕於寶雞，武皇自河中遣使上章，請車駕還京，且言大軍止誅凶黨。

translations.literal: First month of the second year of Guangqi, Emperor Xizong halted at Baoji; Wuhuang from Hezhong sent envoys with a memorial asking that the imperial carriage return to the capital and stating that his great army would punish only the evil clique.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Guangqi 2, with Xizong at Baoji, Wuhuang wrote from Hezhong asking him to return to Chang'an and promising to punish only the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時田令孜請僖宗南幸興元，武皇遂班師。

translations.literal: At the time Tian Lingzi urged Xizong to go south to Xingyuan; Wuhuang then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi persuaded Xizong to go south to Xingyuan, and Wuhuang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朱玫於鳳翔立嗣襄王煴為帝，以偽詔賜武皇，武皇燔之，械其使，馳檄諸方鎮，遣使奉表於行在。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei at Fengxiang enthroned the heir Prince of Xiang Li Yun as emperor, sent a forged edict to bestow on Wuhuang; Wuhuang burned it, put the envoy in fetters, issued proclamations to the regional commands, and sent envoys with a loyal memorial to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei set up Li Yun, Prince of Xiang, as emperor at Fengxiang and sent a forged edict to Wuhuang; Wuhuang burned it, chained the envoy, notified the provinces, and wrote to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 九月，武皇遣昭義節度使李克修討孟方立於邢州，大敗方立之眾於焦崗，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Wuhuang sent the Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Kexiu to attack Meng Fangli at Xing prefecture; at Jiaogang he crushed Fangli's host, beheading several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he sent Li Kexiu of Zhaoyi against Meng Fangli at Xingzhou; at Jiaogang Kexiu routed Fangli and took several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 以大將安金俊為邢州刺史，以撫其降人。

translations.literal: He made the great general An Jinjun prefect of Xing and used him to pacify those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He installed the general An Jinjun as prefect of Xing to pacify the surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十月，進攻邢州，邢人出戰，又敗之。

translations.literal: Tenth month, he pressed the attack on Xing; the Xing men came out to fight and were again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he besieged Xing; the defenders sallied and were beaten again.

sentences.zh: 盂方立求援於鎮州，鎮人出兵三萬以援方立，克修班師。

translations.literal: Meng Fangli begged aid from Zhen prefecture; the Zhen men sent thirty thousand to relieve Fangli, and Kexiu withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli called on Zhenzhou for help; thirty thousand men came to his aid and Kexiu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年六月，河中節度使王重榮為部將常行儒所殺，武皇表重榮兄重盈為帥。

translations.literal: Sixth month of the third year of Guangqi, Wang Chongrong, military commissioner of Hezhong, was killed by his officer Chang Xingru; Wuhuang memorialized that Chongrong's elder brother Chongying be made commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangqi 3 the Hezhong commissioner Wang Chongrong was murdered by his officer Chang Xingru; Wuhuang asked that his brother Chongying succeed him.

sentences.zh: 七月，武皇以安金俊為澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Seventh month, Wuhuang made An Jinjun prefect of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he made An Jinjun prefect of Ze.

sentences.zh: 時張全義自河陽據澤州，及李罕之收復河陽，召全義令守洛陽，全義乃棄澤州而去，故以金俊守之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Quanyi held Ze prefecture from Heyang; when Li Hanzhi recovered Heyang he summoned Quanyi to guard Luoyang, and Quanyi abandoned Ze prefecture and left, so Jinjun was put to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi had seized Ze from Heyang; when Li Hanzhi retook Heyang he called Quanyi to Luoyang, Quanyi abandoned Ze, and Jinjun was stationed there.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年五月，遣李罕之、李存孝攻邢州。

translations.literal: Fifth month of the first year of Longji, he sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao to attack Xing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Longji 1 he sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao against Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，下磁州。

translations.literal: Sixth month, they took Ci prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they took Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 邢將馬溉率兵數萬來拒戰，罕之敗之於琉璃陂，生擒馬溉，徇於城下。

translations.literal: The Xing general Ma Gai led tens of thousands to resist; Hanzhi defeated him at Liuli Slope, captured Ma Gai alive, and displayed him below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gai of Xing brought tens of thousands to the fight; Hanzhi beat him at Liuli Slope, took him alive, and paraded him before the city.

sentences.zh: 孟方立恚恨，飲鴆而死。

translations.literal: Meng Fangli, resentful and enraged, drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Fangli, in despair, took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 三軍立其侄遷為留後，使求援於汴。

translations.literal: The three armies installed his nephew Qian as acting commander and sent to Bian for aid.
translations.idiomatic: The army made his nephew Qian acting commander and asked Bian for help.

sentences.zh: 汴將王虔裕率精甲數百入於邢州，罕之等班師。

translations.literal: The Bian general Wang Qianyu led several hundred picked horsemen into Xing prefecture; Hanzhi and the others withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianyu of Bian entered Xing with several hundred elite horsemen; Hanzhi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月，潞州軍亂，殺節度使李克恭，州人推牙將安居受為留後，南結汴將。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the Lu army mutinied, killed the military commissioner Li Kegong, and the prefectural men pushed the junior officer An Jushou as acting commander, allying south with the Bian commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Lu garrison killed commissioner Li Kegong; the men made the junior officer An Jushou acting commander and turned to Bian.

sentences.zh: 時潞之小將馮霸擁叛徒三千騎駐於沁水，居受使人召之，馮霸不至。

translations.literal: At the time the Lu junior officer Feng Ba held three thousand rebel horsemen at Qinshui; Jushou sent men to summon him, but Feng Ba did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba, a Lu officer, held three thousand mutinous horsemen at Qinshui; Jushou summoned him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 居受懼，出奔至長子，為村胥所殺，傳首於霸；

translations.literal: Jushou was afraid, fled to Changzi, and was killed by a village headman, who sent his head to Feng Ba;
translations.idiomatic: Jushou fled in fear to Changzi, where a village headman killed him and sent his head to Feng Ba;

sentences.zh: 霸遂入潞州，自為留後。

translations.literal: Feng Ba then entered Lu prefecture and made himself acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba then entered Lu and declared himself acting commander.

sentences.zh: 武皇遣大將康君立、李存孝等攻之，汴將朱崇節、葛從周率兵入潞州以固之。

translations.literal: Wuhuang sent the great generals Kang Junli and Li Cunxiao to attack him; the Bian generals Zhu Chongjie and Ge Congzhou led troops into Lu prefecture to reinforce it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Kang Junli and Li Cunxiao against him; Zhu Chongjie and Ge Congzhou of Bian marched into Lu to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 是時，幽州李匡威、雲州赫連鐸與汴帥協謀，連上表請加兵於太原，宰相張浚、孔緯讚成其事。

translations.literal: At the time Li Kuangwei of Youzhou and Helian Duo of Yunzhou plotted with the Bian commander, jointly memorializing again and again to add troops against Taiyuan; the chancellors Zhang Jun and Kong Wei approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou and Helian Duo of Yunzhou joined Zhu Wen in urging the court to reinforce the campaign against Taiyuan; Zhang Jun and Kong Wei backed them.

sentences.zh: 六月，天子削奪武皇官爵，以張浚為招討使，以京兆尹孫揆為副，華州韓建為行營都虞候，以汴帥為河東南面招討使，幽州李匡威為河東北面招討使，雲州赫連鐸為副。

translations.literal: Sixth month, the Son of Heaven stripped Wuhuang of rank and office, made Zhang Jun commander of the punitive campaign and Sun Kui of the capital auxiliary, Han Jian of Huazhou chief of staff of the field army, the Bian commander southern punitive commissioner against Hedong, Li Kuangwei of Youzhou northern punitive commissioner against Hedong, and Helian Duo of Yunzhou his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor degraded Wuhuang, made Zhang Jun commander of the expedition with Sun Kui as deputy and Han Jian as chief of staff, Zhu Wen southern commissioner against Hedong, Li Kuangwei northern commissioner, and Helian Duo his deputy.

sentences.zh: 汴將朱友裕將兵屯晉、絳，時汴軍已據潞州，又遣大將李讜等率軍數萬，急攻澤州，武皇遣李存孝自潞州將三千騎以援之。

translations.literal: The Bian general Zhu Youyu led troops to camp at Jin and Jiang; by then the Bian army already held Lu prefecture, and he also sent the great general Li Dan and others with tens of thousands to press the attack on Ze prefecture; Wuhuang sent Li Cunxiao from Lu with three thousand horsemen to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youyu of Bian encamped at Jin and Jiang; Bian already held Lu, and Li Dan and others were hurrying tens of thousands against Ze; Wuhuang sent Li Cunxiao from Lu with three thousand horsemen to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 汴將鄧季筠以一軍犯陣，存孝追擊，擒其都將十數人，獲馬千餘匹。

translations.literal: Bian general Deng Jiyun led one army to strike the formation; Cunxiao pursued, captured more than ten of his commanders, and seized over a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Bian general Deng Jiyun led a detachment against the line; Li Cunxiao pursued, took a dozen of his commanders, and captured more than a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 是夜，李讜收軍而退，大軍掩擊至馬牢關，斬首萬餘級，追襲至懷州而還。

translations.literal: That night Li Dang withdrew his army; the main force ambushed in pursuit to Malao Pass, beheaded more than ten thousand, and pursued as far as Huai Prefecture before returning.
translations.idiomatic: That night Li Dang pulled back; the main army struck in pursuit to Malao Pass, took more than ten thousand heads, and chased as far as Huai Prefecture before turning back.

sentences.zh: 存孝復引軍攻潞州。

translations.literal: Cunxiao again led troops to attack Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao again marched on Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八月，存孝擒新授昭義節度使孫揆。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Cunxiao captured the newly appointed Zhaoyi military commissioner Sun Kui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Li Cunxiao captured the newly appointed Zhaoyi military commissioner Sun Kui.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷授揆節鉞，以本軍取刀黃嶺路赴任，存孝偵知之，引騎三百伏於長子縣崖穀間。

translations.literal: At first the court invested Kui with credentials; he was to take his own troops by the Daohuang Ridge route to his post. Cunxiao learned of it and led three hundred horsemen to lie in ambush in the cliff ravines of Changzi county.
translations.idiomatic: The court had given Kui his commission and ordered him to take his troops by the Daohuang Ridge road to his post. Cunxiao learned of it, led three hundred cavalry, and hid in the cliff gorges of Changzi.

sentences.zh: 揆建牙持節，褒衣大蓋，擁眾而行，存孝突出穀口，遂擒揆及中使韓歸範，並將校五百人。

translations.literal: Kui raised his command standard with credentials, wore broad robes and a great canopy, and marched with a large retinue. Cunxiao burst from the ravine mouth, captured Kui and the palace envoy Han Guifan, and five hundred officers and troops.
translations.idiomatic: Kui went forth with his insignia, broad robes, and a great canopy, surrounded by his train. Cunxiao rushed from the gorge, seized Kui and the palace envoy Han Guifan, and five hundred officers and men.

sentences.zh: 存孝械揆等，以組練係之，環於潞州，遂獻於武皇。

translations.literal: Cunxiao shackled Kui and the others, bound them with silk cords, displayed them around Lu Prefecture, and then presented them to Wuhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao put Kui and the rest in fetters, tied them with cords, paraded them around Lu Prefecture, and sent them to Wuhuang.

sentences.zh: 武皇謂揆曰：「公搢紳之士，安言徐步可至達官，何用如是！

translations.literal: Wuhuang said to Kui: "You are a court gentleman—who says slow steps cannot reach high office? Why go to such lengths!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang told Kui, "You are a court gentleman; they say a man need only walk slowly to reach high rank—why trouble yourself like this!"

sentences.zh: 」揆無以對，令係於晉陽獄。

translations.literal: 」Kui had no reply; he was ordered confined in the Jinyang prison.
translations.idiomatic: 」Kui could not answer and was confined in the Jinyang prison.

sentences.zh: 武皇將用為副使，使人誘之，揆言不遜，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Wuhuang intended to use him as deputy, sent men to win him over; Kui's words were insolent, and he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang meant to make him his deputy and sent men to win him over; Kui answered insolently and was executed.

sentences.zh: 九月，汴將葛從周棄潞州而遁，武皇以康君立為潞州節度使，以李存孝為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Bian general Ge Congzhou abandoned Lu Prefecture and fled. Wuhuang made Kang Junli military commissioner of Lu and Li Cunxiao prefect of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Ge Congzhou of Bian abandoned Lu and fled. Wuhuang made Kang Junli military commissioner of Lu and Li Cunxiao prefect of Fen.

sentences.zh: 十月，張浚之師入晉州，遊軍至汾、隰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Zhang Jun's army entered Jin Prefecture; patrol troops reached Fen and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhang Jun's army entered Jin Prefecture and scouting parties reached Fen and Xi.

sentences.zh: 武皇遣薛鐵山、李承嗣將騎三千出陰地關，營於洪洞，遣李存孝將兵五千，營於趙城。

translations.literal: Wuhuang sent Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi with three thousand cavalry out through Yindi Pass to camp at Hongdong, and Li Cunxiao with five thousand troops to camp at Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi with three thousand horse out Yindi Pass to camp at Hongdong, and Li Cunxiao with five thousand men to camp at Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 華州韓建以壯士三百人冒犯存孝之營，存孝追擊，直壓晉州西門，張浚之師出戰，為存孝所敗，自是閉壁不出。

translations.literal: Han Jian of Huazhou led three hundred stalwarts against Cunxiao's camp; Cunxiao pursued, pressed straight to the west gate of Jin Prefecture; Zhang Jun's army came out to fight and was defeated by Cunxiao—after that they closed the walls and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian of Huazhou sent three hundred picked men against Cunxiao's camp; Cunxiao pursued them to the west gate of Jin Prefecture. When Zhang Jun's army came out to fight, Cunxiao routed it; from then on they shut the walls and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 存孝引軍攻絳州。

translations.literal: Cunxiao led troops to attack Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao marched on Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二月，晉州刺史張行恭棄城而奔，韓建、張浚由含山路遁去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jin prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled; Han Jian and Zhang Jun escaped by the Hanshan route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jin prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled; Han Jian and Zhang Jun slipped away by the Hanshan road.

sentences.zh: 大順二年春正月，武皇上章申理，其略曰：「臣今身無官爵，名是罪人，不敢歸陛下藩方，且欲於河中寄寓，進退行止，伏候聖裁。

translations.literal: In spring, first month of Datong 2, Wuhuang memorialized in his own defense, in summary: "Your servant now has no office or rank and his name is that of a criminal; he dares not return to Your Majesty's border circuit, and wishes rather to lodge temporarily at Hezhong; whether to advance or withdraw, he awaits the sacred decision."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in Datong 2, Wuhuang memorialized in his own defense, saying in summary: "Your servant now holds no office and bears the name of a criminal; I dare not return to my circuit under Your Majesty and wish instead to lodge at Hezhong for a time; my movements await the sacred decision."

sentences.zh: 」天子尋就加守中書令。

translations.literal: 」The Son of Heaven soon added to his titles Acting Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor soon made him acting chief councilor.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：二月，復拜克用河東節度使、隴西郡王，加檢校太師、兼中書令。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Ouyang History》: In the second month Keyong was again appointed military governor of Hedong and Prince of Longxi, and promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Chancellor of the Secretariat.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang's history says: In the second month Keyong was again made military governor of Hedong and Prince of Longxi, with the added titles of honorary Grand Preceptor and chief councilor.)〉

sentences.zh: 是月，魏博為汴將葛從周所寇，節度使羅宏信遣使來求援，武皇出師以赴之。

translations.literal: That month Weibo was raided by Bian general Ge Congzhou; military commissioner Luo Hongxin sent envoys to beg aid, and Wuhuang marched out to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: That month Ge Congzhou of Bian raided Weibo; military commissioner Luo Hongxin sent envoys asking for help, and Wuhuang marched to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 三月，邢州節度使安知建叛，奔青州。

translations.literal: In the third month Xing military commissioner An Zhijian rebelled and fled to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xing military commissioner An Zhijian rebelled and fled to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天子以知建為神武統軍，自棣州溯河歸朝。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven made Zhijian commander of the Divine Martial Army and ordered him to return to court by river upstream from Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him commander of the Divine Martial Army and ordered him to return to court up the river from Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鄆州朱瑄邀斬於河上，傳首晉陽。

translations.literal: Yanzhou's Zhu Xuan intercepted and beheaded him on the river, and sent the head to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan of Yanzhou cut him down on the river and sent his head to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 以李存孝為邢州節度使。

translations.literal: Li Cunxiao was made military commissioner of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxiao was made military commissioner of Xing.

sentences.zh: 四月，武皇大舉兵討赫連鐸於雲州，遣騎將薛阿檀率前軍以進攻，武皇設伏兵於御河之上，大破之，因塹守其城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army to attack Helian Tuo at Yun Prefecture, sent cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to advance the assault; Wuhuang set ambush troops above the Yu River, routed them utterly, and thereby besieged the city with trenches.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army against Helian Tuo at Yunzhou, sent the cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to press the attack, and set ambushers along the Yu River; he broke Tuo utterly and then walled the city in.

sentences.zh: 七月，武皇進軍柳會，赫連鐸力屈食盡，奔於吐渾部，遂歸幽州，雲州平。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Tuo, strength exhausted and provisions spent, fled to the Tuyuhun, then went to You Prefecture; Yun Prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Tuo, out of strength and food, fled to the Tuyuhun and then to Youzhou; Yunzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 武皇表石善友為大同軍防禦使。

translations.literal: Wuhuang memorialized that Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of the Datong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang memorialized that Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of the Datong Army.

sentences.zh: 邢州節度使李存孝以鎮州王熔托附汴人，謀亂河朔，北連燕寇，請乘雲、代之捷，平定燕、趙，武皇然之。

translations.literal: Xing military commissioner Li Cunxiao, because Zhen's Wang Rong had entrusted himself to Bian, plotted to throw Hebei into disorder and link with northern Yan raiders; he asked to use the victory at Yun and Dai to pacify Yan and Zhao; Wuhuang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxiao of Xing, seeing that Wang Rong of Zhen had thrown in with Bian, plotted to stir trouble in Hebei and ally with Yan in the north; he asked to use the Yun and Dai victories to pacify Yan and Zhao, and Wuhuang agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月，大搜於晉陽，遂南巡澤、潞，略地懷、孟，河陽趙克裕望風送款，請修鄰好。

translations.literal: In the eighth month a great hunt was held at Jinyang; then he toured south through Ze and Lu, overran the lands of Huai and Meng; Heyang's Zhao Keyu submitted at the first rumor of his approach and asked for neighborly peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he held a great hunt at Jinyang, then marched south through Ze and Lu and overran Huai and Meng; Zhao Keyu of Heyang submitted at his approach and asked for peace between neighbors.

sentences.zh: 九月，蒐於邢州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month a hunt at Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he hunted at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，李存孝董前軍攻臨城，鎮人五萬營於臨城西北龍尾崗。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao directed the vanguard to attack Lincheng; fifty thousand Zhen troops encamped at Longwei Ridge northwest of Lincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao led the vanguard against Lincheng; fifty thousand men of Zhen camped on Longwei Ridge northwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 武皇令李存審、李存賢以步軍攻之，鎮人大敗，殺獲萬計，拔臨城，進攻元氏。

translations.literal: Wuhuang ordered Li Cunshen and Li Cunxian with foot troops to attack them; the Zhen army was badly defeated, with tens of thousands killed or captured; Lincheng was taken and the attack pressed on Yuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Li Cunshen and Li Cunxian with infantry against them; the Zhen army was routed, with tens of thousands killed or taken; Lincheng fell and the attack moved on Yuanshi.

sentences.zh: 幽州李匡威以步騎五萬營於鄗邑，以援鎮州，武皇分兵大掠，旋軍邢州。

translations.literal: Youzhou's Li Kuangwei with fifty thousand foot and horse encamped at Hao town to relieve Zhen; Wuhuang divided his forces for wide plunder and then turned the army back to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou camped at Hao with fifty thousand foot and horse to relieve Zhen; Wuhuang split his forces for wide raiding and then wheeled back to Xingzhou.
